paragraphs: Friend, here's what this psalm teaches me. You can trust the LORD and still be a mess. David says "But I trust in You, O LORD," right after he says his bones are wasting away and his friends flee when they see him (Psalm 31:10, 11, 14). Trust didn't mean he never hurt. It meant he took the hurt to the right place.

Now look at where he puts everything. "Into Your hands I commit my spirit," and then, "My times are in Your hands" (Psalm 31:5, 15). He handed over his spirit and his times, and the LORD can carry both. Jesus prayed that first line to His Father from the cross, so these words have carried more than David (Luke 23:46). I can't even carry an oven timer, so I'm VERY glad the big stuff isn't riding on me.

And here's the part I love. David says, "I am cut off from Your sight!" and then admits the LORD heard his plea for mercy anyway (Psalm 31:22). Feeling cut off isn't the same as being cut off. So the next time the dark gets loud, baker, call out to Him, and then do what David says: "Be strong and courageous, all you who hope in the LORD" (Psalm 31:24).
